basis: Inherited heme metabolism disorders; cutaneous and neurologic damage vary by subtype and are not established across most of the umbrella.
Intestinal atresia/enterocolitis and combined immunodeficiency define disease; intrinsic liver damage is not established in >=30%, independently of nutritional treatment.
Developmental disability, seizures and ataxia are characteristic; cutaneous neurofibromas and toenail dysplasia are annotated frequent (30–79%).
The disease itself is irreversible platinum-induced cochlear injury with sensorineural hearing loss.
Inherited macular edema and atrophy cause progressive visual impairment.
Microphthalmia, microtia and arthrogryposis define syndrome; cardiac defects occur in 80–99%. Frequent urinary and duodenal malformations omitted because of cap.
Congenital localized skin absence defines ACC. Very frequent skull/spinal HPO annotations conflict with the definition and usual phenotype; associated defects are a minority.
Malignant germ cell tumor originating in the stomach.
Hepatic heme synthesis disorder; blistering photosensitive skin injury affects roughly half of symptomatic patients. Persistent neuropathy is less common.
Congenital malformation of the atrioventricular septum and associated valves.
Respiratory ciliary dysfunction causes chronic airway disease; recurrent otitis media affects 9/11 patients (~82%). Situs inversus alone does not damage organs.
Fibrohistiocytic neoplasm arising in the dermis.
Alopecia universalis is the generalized autoimmune form of alopecia areata, causing loss of scalp and body hair.
Kyphoscoliosis, hypotonia and joint instability define disease; skin fragility/scarring and hypermetropia each occur in 30–79%. Vascular rupture/hearing loss are minority features.
Generalized congenital subcutaneous fat loss with metabolic dysfunction; hepatic steatosis affects most generalized lipodystrophy patients (>50%); subtype-specific data limited.
Skeletal dysplasia and dysautonomia define syndrome; corneal sensory dysfunction with visual impairment is very frequent (80–99%). Respiratory episodes reflect dysautonomia.
Anterior segment maldevelopment defines ocular disease; unspecified extraocular manifestations do not establish another organ axis.
Mitochondrial disorder with cardiomyopathy (4/4); hepatic injury ~80%, developmental delay characteristic (documented 1/1). Single reported renal lesion omitted at cap.
Mitochondrial encephalomyopathy with neurodegeneration, neuropathy and muscle wasting in nearly all; respiratory failure is attributable to muscle weakness.
Phosphofructokinase deficiency directly affects skeletal muscle glycolysis and erythrocytes, causing metabolic myopathy and hemolytic anemia.
Inherited surfactant metabolism disorders cause alveolar accumulation and impaired gas exchange; autoimmunity is not the mechanism of this hereditary umbrella.
Epiphyseal stippling, ocular colobomata and developmental delay characterize syndrome; reported cardiac malformations lack an established >=30% frequency.
Congenital ophthalmoplegia, ptosis, miosis and associated amblyopia define ocular dysfunction; no separate neurologic lesion is established.
Primary carcinoma of the peritoneal lining; ovarian and fallopian tube origins are explicitly excluded.
Pulmonary lymphatic maldevelopment causes lung and pleural disease; chylopericardium directly involves the pericardium in 30–79%. Reflux is a separate disease.
